learning_outcomes.text: Possess advanced knowledge and skills (critical understanding of theories and principles) in the field of modern Photonics, with emphasis on modern applications, like in telecommunications and nano-photonics.
Be able to use the knowledge acquired in a way that shows a professional approach to their work.
Be able to gather and interpret elements of the subject to form scientifically documented opinion, both on scientific and social/ethical issues (e.g., risks of new technologies to human health).
Be able to communicate information and solutions to the subject of the course (modern photonic materials) to both a specialized and non-specialized audience.
Have developed knowledge-acquiring skills, which they need to pursue further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Analytical and synthetic ability to solve problems.
Manage complex physical theories and mathematical techniques.
Bibliographic research, analysis, synthesis and presentation of contemporary research findings.

syllabus_topics: Light and matter, light waves, absorption and emission, optical properties of matter
Optics of short laser pulses: theory and applications
Nonlinear optics: materials, systems and spatio-temporal phenomena
teaching_methods: Use of Information and Communications Technology (ICT) in delivery and communication with students

assessment_methods.method: Active participation in the class (questions and quizzes)

assessment_rules: Student performance is evaluated through active class participation (questions and quizzes) contributing 10% to the final grade, homework/presentations contributing 30%, and a research project contributing 60%. Evaluation methods can be conducted in Greek or English.
bibliography: Fundamentals of Photonics, B.E.A. Saleh and M.C. Teich, 2nd edition Wiley
Photonics, A. Yariv and P. Yeh, 6th edition Oxford University Press
degree: Materials Science and Engineering — Πτυχίο Τμήματος Επιστήμης και Μηχανικής Υλικών (first cycle, 240 ECTS, curriculum ΕΜΥ)
